rows.notes: SMM 2026-04-27: designed to process 300,000 t/yr spent LFP batteries, investment 1.066 bn yuan (headline mis-states USD). One other SMM item gives 30,000 t for the same project (search summary) - possible typo/conflict; EIA draft out for comment 2026-06-03 (search summary). Status announced (EIA/permitting stage; the headline says 'launches' but no construction evidence).

fields.asset_name: POSCO HY Clean Metal Gwangyang (Yulchon) battery recycling plant
fields.product: lithium carbonate, nickel/cobalt/manganese sulphates (from black mass)

rows.notes: Herald (2026-11-10): 12,000 t/yr black mass (input), 2,500 t/yr lithium carbonate, lithium-carbonate line at >95% utilisation. 2023 sources: from 12,000 t recovers 2,500 t Ni, 800 t Co, 2,500 t Li2CO3; Oct 2026 Maeil Business gives 12,000 t NiSO4, 3,800 t CoSO4, 2,000 t MnSO4 (sulphate vs metal basis; search summaries). Start year 2023 and Huayou JV partner from search summaries/2023 coverage, not opened. POSCO Poland (Legnica) sourcing centre produces ~8,000 t/yr black mass (search summary) - not added.

fields.asset_name: SungEel HiTech Saemangeum No. 3 (3rd Hydro Center), Gunsan

rows.notes: CONFLICT: SMM 2026-02-26 gives 20,000 t/yr and ~90% utilisation (S46); Asia Economy 2024-07-02 says the 3rd Hydro Center, completed early June 2024, can process 40,000 t/yr on black powder input (S47). Unresolved - the 20,000 t figure (later, more specific) is used; the 40,000 t may be a design/phase-2 or scope difference. 2022 IPO plan was 10,000 t. Start 2024 from the asiae completion report. SungEel's older Gunsan plants and LFP pilot (~500 t) not added.

fields.asset_name: Sumitomo Metal Mining LIB recycling (Toyo Works, Saijo + Niihama Nickel Refinery)
fields.product: nickel, cobalt, lithium, copper recovered (dry + wet process)

rows.notes: Business Journal (2026-09-23): the two sites (Toyo dry, Niihama wet) are linked to process about 10,000 t/yr of used batteries (battery-cell basis); completion ceremony at the Toyo Works on Sept 11 (year not in body text; article 2026). One row for the two-site process (capacity not allocated between sites). Earlier targets: Nikkan Kogyo (2023-06): 'aim for ~10,000 t/yr'; Argus 2024 quoted ~6,000-7,000 t/yr black mass (search summary). Completed later than the planned June 2026.

fields.asset_name: Attero Recycling Roorkee (Uttarakhand) lithium-ion battery recycling

rows.notes: EVreporter interview (Dec 2024): ~15,000 t/yr of battery recycling at full capacity; main plant Roorkee. Argus (search summary): 15,000 t/yr Li-ion and ~144,000 t/yr e-waste; plans 100,000 t/yr Li-ion plant in Andhra Pradesh and 200,000 t/yr target (not added - no opened source). BDO India estimate 17,500 t/yr (ThePrint via search summary) - conflict. Industry total India ~50-60 kt/yr (search summary).

Fastmarkets (2024-02-12): input capacity 20,000 t battery scrap, can produce 10,000 t/yr black mass. Plant location (Greater Noida, UP) not confirmed by the opened page, so province null. Earlier ~1,000 t/yr and BDO India 20,000 t (ThePrint via search summary). Lohum also has a battery-grade lithium refinery plan (~1 Mtpa per search summary; not verified) - belongs in refining.

Minister's speech at the official opening of TES-B (2021-03-24): annual capacity 5,000 t of Li-ion batteries (14 t/day per search summary). Operating since 2021 per the opening event (status inferred from 'official opening' speech); current utilisation unknown. Government later cited other Singapore EV battery recyclers at 8,600 t combined plus KGS 2,600 t/yr (search summary). Green Li-ion (Singapore): no source found.

fields.asset_name: BEEAH-Lohum (MoEI) EV battery recycling facility, Al Saja'a, Sharjah
fields.jv_partners: BEEAH; Lohum; UAE Ministry of Energy and Infrastructure (MoEI)

rows.notes: BEEAH release 2026-01-15: JV aims to develop the facility in 2026 with 1,500 t/yr, doubling by year 3 (so ~3,000 t/yr by about 2028-29; doubling not captured in capacity). Output black mass for Lohum's Indian refining (search summary). Not verified whether construction has begun by Nov 2026. [lead] confidence capped at 0.5: key field rests on reported evidence.

fields.asset_name: Witthal Gulf Industries lithium battery recycling plant (KEZAD, Abu Dhabi)
fields.jv_partners: KEZAD Group (Khalifa Economic Zones Abu Dhabi)

rows.notes: Zawya Projects (undated): 5,000 t/yr, full operations Q2 2027; partners KEZAD Group and Witthal Gulf Industries. KEZAD partner role (JV vs landlord) not clear from the page; exact site not stated. An energy-solutions.co claim of >150,000 t/yr combined UAE/Saudi capacity is uncorroborated and ignored.
